text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Competition in Denmark between credit companies offering loan cards is mounting with ever-increasing involvement by foreign banks forced into Scandinavia by saturated home markets and eager to win over Danish private bank customers, threatening local banks.

--- Danish telecommunications group Teledanmark is considering starting up its own TV entertainment programme production operation after negotiations on taking over Danish film producer Metronome along with Norwegian media group Schibsted collapsed.

--- The artificial Ecstasy drug seems to have gained ground in Copenhagen dance clubs and sources now estimate that close on 1,000 pills are sold every weekend. So far Copenhagen police have only confiscated 91 pills this year, admitting that they do not know how widespread the drug's use is or how it is being smuggled into Denmark.

--- A new survey by the Wonderful Copenhagen tourist promotion organisation shows that six major international conferences, bringing in some 350 million crowns in earnings and creating over 1,000 jobs, have had to be turned down due to lack of hotel/conference centre capacity in the Danish capital.
